design.scope: Assume retaining four lanes preserves the canopy; test traffic performance only. Canopy preservation is an input assumption, not a simulated finding.
design.data: GDOT station 121-0312, April 1 and 2 2025; provisional reported-unit-to-vehicle interpretation retained from the audit. Other link volumes inherit historical spatial ratios.
design.training: Select each road size's AM and PM plan using April 1, seed 0, nominal saturation 1800 and side demand 450. Freeze those plans for April 2 and all stress cases. This is a held-out input-day check, not validation against measured delays.
design.selection: Among candidates with peak hourly movement v/c <= 1, side mean delay <= 90 seconds and full drainage, minimize all-trip mean queue delay. If none qualify, report no qualifying candidate; retain the minimum-delay candidate only as a labelled diagnostic.

comparison_screen.description: Illustrative research thresholds, not engineering approval or official standards. Evaluate seed-mean results and report individual-seed variation separately.

design.uncertainties: Saturation 1600/1800; side demand 450/650; main and side growth 10/20/30 percent; 35 mph travel against frozen 40 mph offsets; +15 percent volume on unobserved links; 10/20 percent main-demand reduction under combined stress. These are scenarios, not forecasts, probabilities or predicted program effects.
design.analytical_envelope: Independently compute the necessary green-time budget using capacity = lane-group saturation * effective green / cycle. Evaluate v/c targets of 1.0 and 0.9. This ignores turning phases, storage losses and pedestrian constraints, so it is an optimistic upper bound, not proof of sufficiency.
